image.alt: A doctor wearing a stethoscope checks a patient's blood pressure; the patient has offered their forearm, which is bound in an inflatable cuff, while the doctor rests the bell on the forearmFile photo dated 10/09/14 of a GP checking a patient's blood pressure. Only half of people being treated by their GP for high blood pressure have it under control, according to new data for England. Analysis by Oxford University of 1.4 million adults also found most people across England with the condition are unaware they have it, increasing their risk of stroke, heart attack and early death. cards.headline: From paleo to intermittent fasting: are any diets actually good for us?

image.alt: As diet trends proliferate on social media, it can be hard to work out which are backed by science and which should be ignored. From paleo to keto, raw food to intermittent fasting, each attracts a tribe of ardent followers. Now Daniel Lieberman, professor of biological sciences at Harvard University, has written a book to try to cut through the noise. In Fed Up, he uses his background as an evolutionary anthropologist to scrutinise the evidence, turning himself into a guinea pig in the process and trying various diets. In this podcast, he tells Ian Sample which one has remained part of his routine
